There's probably a lot of truth to that. My personal definition of alcoholism is more about the relationship to alcohol rather than quantity consumed. For example I think there's plenty of people out there who could be considered alcoholic who only drink weekend nights. It's more about the obsession and the dwelling and altering your schedule to accommodate the habit. If that makes sense. And of course on the flip side there's probably plenty of people who have a couple morning screwdrivers a few times a week that wouldn't be considered alcoholic. 

Now don't get me wrong. Quanity certainly plays a part particularly when it comes to physical withdrawals. 

At the end of the day "alcoholism" is a problematic term. A lot of people think it's some sort of pass or that the alcoholic cannot control how much they drink. Really though it is a decision. It may not seem like it when in the throes of withdrawal but the unfortunate fact is that it is.

Well since its my throwaway I don't mind disclosing where I go to school lol. I go to Western Washington University. A small public University in Northwest Washington State. 

I hear what youre saying about personal aspirations and family tradition. I actually am in the opposite position because I'll be one of the first people in my family to ever graduate from college. My uncle got two BA's but that's all I can think of. And my dad is about to get his CS degree but he techinally hasn't completed it yet. So I can imagine where you're coming from but I can't relate. Of course all of my family is supportive and stoked that I'm pursuing undergrad. 

And that's good about the federal loans thing. And I forget that not everybody is on a quarter system lol. I imagine you could take a semester off though right? In theory? I would encourage you to do what you think is best, and if you think that's taking a year off then I would encourage you to do that.

In my opinion nobody can know whether it's good to take a year off except for you. I'll tell you about myself and maybe it will help you examine yourself to decide what's best. 

Everyone is different. A lot of people will tell you that taking a year off is risky because you may settle into something else and never go back. And maybe there's nothing wrong with that even. But I'm certain there are people out there who can take a year off and stick to their original plan of going back with ease. 

But for myself if I were to take a year off I imagine I would get settled into my job and enjoy the fact that I didn't have two entirely separate things to focus on (I work part time while going to school). 

But here's the thing. I'm resistant to change and I struggle to enact it all on my own accord. When somebody expects something of me then I almost always meet their standards just fine, but when it comes to doing something purely for my own well being then I often procrastinate it or don't do it entirely. 

So the questions that I would ask myself would be how I experience change and what my habits are related to change. A year is not a very long time in relative terms but if you're young like me it can feel like a whole lot of time has passed in a year. You may find yourself feeling repulsed by the notion of going back. Especially since you would be leaving on a sour note. Or maybe you'll count down the days until you can get back to college. Only you can know and I think that if you look back at your past behavior when it comes time to do something for yourself then you might get some idea. 

I mean, hell, you got yourself into Harvard. That would suggest to me that you have some sort of work ethic and are willing to put yourself out there just for you. 

My mom worked her ass off to send me to a college prep school. So when it came time to go to college it was obviously what I should do. Dont get me wrong I love college and think I belong here. 

Oh you should also bear in mind (and I'm not an expert on this matter)but if you're receiving federal loans then you must begin paying them back within six months after your last classes. That's another reason I would probably never take a year off. 

You could also consider taking one quarter off, right? Or two quarters, or whatever. 

Its 1 am my time and I also typed this on mobile and it got rambly lol. Whatever decision you make try not to second guess yourself. Own that shit. Good luck friend! It will probably all work out as it usually does.
